title: CD200 and CD200R  levels in psoriasis patients
author: Carmen Farid

steps_raw.instruction: Fresh venous blood samples (5ml) were withdrawn for all participants under aseptic conditions; 2.5mls were centrifuged to separate serum, which was stored at -80 °C until samples of patients and control groups were assayed in one run.
Estimation of level of soluble CD200 in the serum was performed with commercially available enzyme linked immune sorbent assay (ELISA) kit.
The other 2.5 ml were used while still fresh for estimation of CD200R by flow cytometry using Human CD200 R1 Fluorescein-conjugated Antibody (BioTech, USA)

Serum levels of CD200 were quantitated with commercially available enzyme linked immune sorbent assay (ELISA) kit (Human CD200 PicoKine™ ELISA Kit, Boster Biological Technology, Pleasanton CA, USA, Catalog # EK0993)
Human CD200 PicoKine™ ELISA Kit is based on standard sandwich enzyme-linked immune-sorbent assay technology. An antibody specific for CD200 has been pre-coated onto 96-well plates.
Standards and test samples are added to the wells, a biotinylated detection antibody specific for CD200 is added subsequently and then followed by washing with PBS buffer.

Avidin-Biotin-Peroxidase Complex was added and unbound conjugates were washed away with PBS buffer. HRP substrate TMB was used to visualize HRP enzymatic reaction. TMB was catalyzed by HRP to produce a blue color product that changed into yellow after adding acidic stop solution. The density of yellow is proportional to the Human CD200 amount of sample captured in plate [1].
Estimation of CD200R in fresh blood samples was performed with floecytometry using human CD200 R1 conjugated antibody.
The expression of CD200R was estimated on peripheral blood monocytes.

EDTA whole blood was stained with mouse Anti-human CD200R1 Fluorescein-conjugated monoclonal antibody (Human CD200 R1 Fluorescein-conjugated Antibody, Bio-Techne, Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA, Catalog # FAB3414F)

Briefly, 100 μL of whole blood were stained with fluorescein-conjugated anti-CD200R. After incubation, 2.0 mL of lysing solution was added and lysis was allowed for 10 min at room temperature. Samples were then washed twice and resuspended in PBS.

Cells were analyzed on a FACSCalibur flow cytometer using CellQuest pro software (BD Biosciences, San Diego, CA, USA). Membrane fluorescence intensity was estimated by the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI).
The MFI of CD200R on peripheral blood monocytes was evaluated in psoriasis patients and healthy controls [2].
1- Wild D. The Immunoassay Handbook: Theory and Applications of Ligand Binding, ELISA and Related Techniques. 4th ed. Amsterdam: Elsevier Science; 2013.
2- Givan AL. Flow Cytometry: First Principles. 2nd ed. Canada: Wiley-Liss; 2001.
